problem: Mainstream VLN assumes instructions perfectly match a fixed navigation graph. Agents trained this way rigidly follow instructions and fail when the real environment differs (closed doors, moved objects, blocked paths).
motivation: Real-world instructions come from prior memory and often mismatch the current environment, e.g. a suitcase blocking a hallway. Humans find detours, but SOTA VLN agents lose about 20-30% SR once a single edge is blocked. Existing obstacle-avoidance work is continuous-setting and focuses on obstacle properties rather than high-level adaptability when instructions fail.
key_idea: Build an obstructed R2R (R2R-UNO) by blocking redundant graph edges and inpainting matching obstructions into the panoramas, then train agents with curriculum sampling of original and obstructed data plus virtual nodes for blocked edges (ObVLN).
insight: Training naively on both original and obstructed data over-optimizes for detours and hurts R2R (DUET +OE: R2R val-unseen SR 72 -> 65, TL 16.74 -> 25.02). Curriculum sampling, which starts with unobstructed data and ramps the obstructed ratio, keeps both. It was the only strategy best on both R2R and R2R-UNO in the sampling ablation (Table 3). Visual obstruction feedback (object insertion plus CLIP/GMM filtering) adds gains (DUET R2R-UNO SR 60.5 -> 64.8 -> 68.5). Virtual nodes close much of the gap to an oracle graph (Block-3 SR 56.3 vanilla, 63.1 ours, 66.2 oracle).
method: R2R-UNO graph changes: find redundant edges on each R2R path whose removal keeps the graph connected; block 1, 2 or 3 of them (Block-1/2/3) and define a new 'real path' via shortest detours, with length limit 10+5x. 98.8% of R2R paths are modified.

Object insertion module: locate the neighbor node in the view via pixel projection, build a right-trapezoid mask along the path, and inpaint an object (Stable Diffusion v1.5 inpainting, 10 categories such as chair, suitcase, dog) with a prompt template.

Filtering module: score each candidate with CLIP (masked region vs object name), fit a 2-component GMM per category (success vs failure peak) to keep good candidates, and fall back to the top 3 scorers if none qualify.
Panorama propagation: SIFT matching (brute force + KNN) between adjacent views projects the inpainted region into the 8 neighboring views for consistency.
Curriculum training: obstructed-sample ratio alpha(t)=min(alpha_max, t/c*alpha_max), with alpha_max=0.5 and c=20K; every batch mixes both data types.

Virtual graph construction (for map-based agents like DUET): when a view is obstructed, create a virtual node at a predefined distance d=3 m; when the agent gets within threshold theta of both the virtual node and the current node while obstruction is seen, link the virtual node to the current node with a zero-weight edge.

setting.backbone: HAMT and DUET (fine-tuned, with ObVLN training)
setting.training_data: R2R train + R2R-UNO (Block-1/2/3 with inpainted views); PREVALENT augmented data; obstructed data used only in fine-tuning; 100K iterations, batch size 8, lr 1e-5, one A6000
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) with heading/elevation features; inpainted obstruction views
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (DUET uses a global topological action space); max action length 30
setting.privileged: none (the oracle graph appears only in an ablation upper bound)

numbers.extra: trained with R2R + R2R-UNO, PREVALENT augmentation

results: Baselines trained on R2R only collapse on R2R-UNO (DUET val-unseen SR 44/31/23 on Block-1/2/3). DUET+ObVLN reaches SR 67/65/63 while keeping R2R val-unseen SR at 72, matching the Basic setting, and it beats plain +OE (65/63/60 on Block-1/2/3; R2R SR 65). Zero-shot evaluation of five SOTA methods (RecBERT, HAMT, DUET, GELA, ScaleVLN) shows SR falling from 60-70% to about 40% with one blocked edge.
limitations: Uses 2D inpainting, which can give multi-view inconsistency; obstructions are only inserted at nodes along blocked edges.
Discrete-graph setting only, with no continuous control or real-robot validation. The virtual graph mechanism is inapplicable to non-map methods like HAMT, and it slightly lowers DUET's SPL on R2R.
